correctness.rationale: For the outer actions, a bimodule map is determined by c=Δ(1) with (a⊗1)c=c(1⊗a). Multiplication by diagonal idempotents leaves only tensors e_ia⊗e_bi, b≤i≤a, in Δ(e_ii). For i≤j both expansions for Δ(e_ij) have coefficients of e_ia⊗e_bj, and if only one side supports a term, the tensor is still a valid basis element and its coefficient must vanish. Thus zero-padded coefficients are constant for fixed (a,b) on each comparability component. A nonzero coefficient forces b and a to bound the whole component and belong to it. Conversely the extremal tensor formula respects the outer actions and both triple coproducts are λ_C² e_xt⊗e_st⊗e_sy. Distinct intervals give distinct basis tensors and distinct components have disjoint supports, proving rank d_C per active component and the product enumerator, including the zero-map/empty-product case. A counit requires injectivity; if s≠t then the left counit on Δ(e_tt) has output proportional to e_st, not e_tt. On singleton components the inverse scalars are counit values. The diamond has nine intervals; in its presentation J³=0 and I is the one-dimensional subspace spanned by the difference of its two distinct length-two paths. It contains neither path, also in characteristic two. Thus it is admissible, has only a binomial relation, and the rank-nine coproduct is a valid witness against the unrestricted literal wording. Inspected VERIFICATION.md and incidence_noncounital_checker.py; the reported 814 finite tests solve the residual linear equations after diagonal reduction over F₂ and F₃. The triple-tensor check restates the symbolic formula and is not independent evidence of coassociativity. No uploaded code was executed.
